nodes.description: GNRHR encodes the type 1 GnRH receptor, a 328-residue class A G protein-coupled receptor of pituitary gonadotropes. It binds the decapeptide GnRH in a pocket formed by the N-terminal segment, the extracellular loops and transmembrane helices 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7, and activates Gq/11. Among mammalian receptors of this class it is unusual in having no cytoplasmic C-terminal tail and no helix 8, in carrying Asn at 2.50 and Asp at 7.49 (the reverse of the usual pair), and in having a DRS motif where most receptors have DRY. Disease alleles are mostly missense variants spread through the whole protein, with fewer nonsense, frameshift and splice variants. Missense alleles range from complete to partial loss of function. The gene is not constrained against loss of function in the population (gnomAD v4.1 LOEUF 0.78, pLI 0.02, missense Z 0.35), as expected for a recessive disorder.

nodes.description: The mutant receptor does not reach its native fold and is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, so little or none arrives at the plasma membrane. This is the most common mechanism among tested missense alleles. The receptors are often intrinsically competent: small cell-permeant antagonists that bind the folding receptor (pharmacoperones) restore surface expression and signalling for most of them in cells, and for E90K in a knock-in mouse. The human receptor is close to the limit of what quality control accepts even when wild type, because of Lys191 in extracellular loop 2, a residue that the rat and mouse receptors lack and that lowers routing to the surface. On the structure, the alleles in this class change buried residues of the helix bundle (for example Glu90 at 2.53, Ala129 at 3.40, Ala171 at 4.57, Leu266 at 6.34, Cys279 at 6.47 and Pro320 at 7.50), or put an arginine on a helix face inside the membrane (Ser168 at 4.54, Ser217 at 5.44).

nodes.description: Alleles at the cytoplasmic ends of helices 3 and 6 and in intracellular loop 2 leave the hormone pocket intact but prevent the active receptor from engaging Gq/11. Arg139 is the arginine of the DRS motif (3.50). In the inactive human structure it is paired with Asp138 and contacts Thr265 and Arg262 on helix 6; in the active pig structure the equivalent arginine is 3.7 angstroms from the Gq alpha subunit. Arg262 (6.30) is 5.2 angstroms from Gq, next to Ala261, Lys264 and Thr265, which touch it, and Pro146 (34.50, intracellular loop 2) is 3.6 angstroms from it. Arg139His also abolishes measurable binding in cells, so this class overlaps with misfolding.

nodes.description: Investigational; not tested in patients. evidence.reference_title: Restoration of testis function in hypogonadotropic hypogonadal mice harboring a misfolded GnRHR mutant by pharmacoperone drug therapy.
evidence.snippet: Spermatogenesis, proteins associated with steroid transport and steroidogenesis, and androgen levels were restored in mutant male mice following pharmacoperone therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Receptor-misrouting: an unexpectedly prevalent and rescuable etiology in gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor-mediated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: We now report that this approach rescues 11 of 13 of these GnRHR missense mutants.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism due to GnRH receptor mutations in three brothers reveal sites affecting conformation and coupling.
evidence.snippet: Pretreatment with the membrane permeant GnRHR antagonist NBI-42902, which rescues cell surface expression of many GNRHR1 mutants, significantly increased the levels of radioligand binding and intracellular signaling of the Tyr323Cys mutant but not Pro282Arg.

nodes.description: Menses do not start. Reported in women with complete and with partial forms, including women whose breast development is normal.

evidence.reference_title: The same molecular defects of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor determine a variable degree of hypogonadism in affected kindred.
evidence.snippet: They both had primary amenorrhea, and the younger sister displayed retarded bone maturation and uterus development, but both sisters had normal breast development.

evidence.reference_title: Successful use of pulsatile gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) for ovulation induction and pregnancy in a patient with GnRH receptor mutations.
evidence.snippet: we studied a kindred in which two sisters with primary amenorrhea were affected with GnRH deficiency due to a compound heterozygote mutation (Gln(106)Arg, Arg(262)Gln)

nodes.description: Bone mass is at risk in untreated or undertreated patients of both sexes, because sex steroids are needed to build and keep it. Bone mineral density is monitored, and calcium and vitamin D intake kept adequate. No GNRHR-specific bone density series was found; this is recorded from guidance for isolated GnRH deficiency as a group, without a frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Optimal calcium and vitamin D intake should be encouraged and specific treatment for decreased bone mass as needed.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: In individuals with confirmed IGD, monitor at regular intervals: serum sex steroid levels (to guide optimal hormone replacement); bone mineral density.

nodes.description: The number of functional receptors on the gonadotrope plasma membrane falls. Receptor number matters for this receptor because GnRH arrives in brief pulses and the size of the LH response follows receptor occupancy.

animal_models.description: Pharmacoperone treatment restores surface receptor and downstream testicular function in vivo.
animal_models.name: Gnrhr E90K knock-in mouse

evidence.reference_title: Molecular basis of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: restoration of mutant (E(90)K) GnRH receptor function by a deletion at a distant site.
evidence.snippet: Activation of intracellular signaling in response to Buserelin was restored by deletion of K(191) from the E(90)K mutant receptor

nodes.description: Alleles in or beside the hormone pocket lower affinity for GnRH without abolishing it, so the dose-response curve shifts to the right and the receptor still signals at high GnRH concentrations. These are typically partial loss-of-function alleles. In the active-state pig receptor structure, the positions equivalent to human Arg38 (1.35), Tyr283 (6.51) and Tyr284 (6.52) are within 4 angstroms of GnRH and Gln174 (4.60) is at 4.1 angstroms; Arg38 is also paired with Asp98 (2.61). Gln106 in extracellular loop 1 is 5.8 angstroms from the hormone, near it but not in contact, and hydrogen-bonds to the backbone of extracellular loop 2. The first 17 residues, which include Asn10, are not resolved in either experimental structure.

evidence.reference_title: Two novel mutations in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor gene in Brazilian patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and normal olfaction.
evidence.snippet: The Asn(10)Lys mutation in the extracellular amino-terminal domain of the receptor also reduced the affinity for GnRH in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: The fertile eunuch variant of idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: spontaneous reversal associated with a homozygous mutation in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor.
evidence.snippet: This mutation, located in the first extracellular loop of the GnRH-R, has been previously shown to decrease but not eliminate GnRH binding.

evidence.reference_title: Genetics of ncHH: from a peculiar inheritance of a novel GNRHR mutation to a comprehensive review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Functional studies for the p.Gly99Glu mutation demonstrated a right-shifted GnRH-stimulated signaling response.

evidence.reference_title: Cryo-EM structures of GnRHR: Foundations for next-generation therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: The conserved "U"-shaped GnRH conformation mediates high-affinity binding through key interactions with residues such as K3.32, Y6.51, and Y6.52.

nodes.description: Gradually increasing doses of testosterone induce and maintain virilization in boys and men. It does not induce spermatogenesis or testicular growth. Because hypogonadism reverses in some patients, most often those with partial loss-of-function alleles, a brief withdrawal of treatment to test for recovery is reasonable; testicular growth during testosterone treatment suggests recovery.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: To induce and maintain secondary sex characteristics, gradually increasing doses of testosterone or human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) injections in males or estrogen and progestin in females

evidence.reference_title: GNRHR-related central hypogonadism with spontaneous recovery - case report.
evidence.snippet: At the age of 19 years, testosterone supplementation was interrupted. During the next two years, he had spontaneous pubertal development to achieve a testicular volume of 20 mL, with normal adult levels of gonadotropins and testosterone.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function. Ala129 (3.40) is in the middle of helix 3, fully buried (relative solvent accessibility 0.04), 15 angstroms from Gq and 11 angstroms from the ligand. An aspartate there puts a charge in the hydrophobic core of the bundle, which is expected to prevent folding. ClinVar: pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: Resistance of hypogonadic patients with mutated GnRH receptor genes to pulsatile GnRH administration.
evidence.snippet: This A129D mutation results in a complete loss of function, indicated by the lack of inositol triphosphate (TP3) 3 production by transfected Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells after GnRH stimulation.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function. Ala171 (4.57) is buried at the interface of helices 3 and 4 (relative solvent accessibility 0.00). The original report modelled a new hydrogen bond from Thr171 to Tyr119 on helix 3 that would lock the two helices together. Ala171Val (ClinVar VCV003660422, likely pathogenic) at the same residue cannot make that bond, which suggests that added bulk at this packed position is enough to disrupt the receptor. ClinVar: pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation Ala(171)Thr stabilizes the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor in its inactive conformation, causing familial hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: Specific receptor binding of (125)I-labeled GnRH ligand was undetectable in Ala(171)Thr GnRH receptor-transfected cells.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation Ala(171)Thr stabilizes the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor in its inactive conformation, causing familial hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: Molecular modeling and dynamic simulation of the Ala(171)Thr GnRH receptor suggests the introduction of a stable hydrogen bond between residue Thr(171) and Tyr(119) side-chains at a distance of 2 A.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function. The arginine of the DRS motif (3.50) at the cytoplasmic end of helix 3. In the inactive human structure it is salt-bridged to Asp138 and contacts Thr265 and Arg262 on helix 6; in the active pig structure the equivalent arginine is 3.7 angstroms from Gq. Histidine cannot make both sets of contacts. gnomAD v4.1 allele frequency 0.00015, no homozygotes. It is one of three GNRHR founder alleles, and Brazilian carriers share a haplotype. ClinVar: pathogenic, multiple submitters. Arg139Cys (ClinVar VCV001675193) is a second pathogenic allele at the same residue.

evidence.reference_title: Two novel mutations in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor gene in Brazilian patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and normal olfaction.
evidence.snippet: The Arg(139)His mutation completely eliminated detectable GnRH-binding activity and prevented GnRH-induced stimulation of inositol phosphate accumulation in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Role of gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor mutations in patients with a wide spectrum of pubertal delay.
evidence.snippet: The founder effect study revealed that Brazilian patients carrying the p.R139H mutation shared the same haplotype.

nodes.description: Partial loss of function through impaired coupling. Cytoplasmic end of helix 6 (6.30). In the inactive human structure Arg262 lies against Arg139 of the DRS motif; in the active pig structure the equivalent arginine is 5.2 angstroms from the Gq alpha subunit. Binding is retained and phospholipase C activation is reduced. gnomAD v4.1 allele frequency 0.0015 with 7 homozygotes. Usually found in compound heterozygosity with a more severe allele; overrepresented among patients whose hypogonadism reverses. A founder allele. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: The same molecular defects of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor determine a variable degree of hypogonadism in affected kindred.
evidence.snippet: When expressed in heterologous cells, both Gln106Arg and Ser217Arg mutations altered hormone binding, whereas the Arg262Gln mutation altered activation of phospholipase C.

evidence.reference_title: Reversible congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in patients with CHD7, FGFR1 or GNRHR mutations.
evidence.snippet: Two reversal variants had a same GNRHR mutation (R262Q), which was accompanied by another GNRHR mutation (R139H or del309F).

nodes.description: Null allele. The stop codon is at the start of helix 1, so no transmembrane domain is made. Homozygous patients have complete disease and heterozygous relatives are unaffected, which shows that half the normal gene dosage is enough. The missense allele Arg38Gln at the same residue (ClinVar VCV003004558, likely pathogenic) removes the arginine that pairs with Asp98 and contacts pGlu1 of GnRH.

evidence.reference_title: Whole Exome Sequencing Revealed a Novel Nonsense Variant in the GNRHR Gene Causing Normosmic Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism in a Pakistani Family.
evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis identified a novel nonsense mutation (chr4: g.68619942G>A, c.112C>T, p.Arg38*) in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor gene (GNRHR) recessively co-segregating with nCHH in this family.

nodes.description: Partial loss of function through reduced affinity. Extracellular N-terminus. This residue is not resolved in 7BR3 or 9U4W and the AlphaFold model has pLDDT 33 here, so no structural reasoning is possible. The N-terminus does enter the binding site in the antagonist-bound crystal structure. gnomAD v4.1 allele frequency 0.00013 for c.30T>A. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: Two novel mutations in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor gene in Brazilian patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and normal olfaction.
evidence.snippet: The Asn(10)Lys mutation in the extracellular amino-terminal domain of the receptor also reduced the affinity for GnRH in vitro.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function. Cys200 is in extracellular loop 2. Mutagenesis literature assigns it a disulfide bond to Cys14 of the N-terminus, in addition to the conserved Cys114-Cys196 bond; Cys14 is not resolved in 7BR3, so the bond cannot be confirmed on experimental coordinates. The AlphaFold model places the two sulfurs 2.0 angstroms apart, a disulfide, but with low confidence in that region (pLDDT 54 at Cys14), and the pig receptor of 9U4W has glycine at position 200. Loss of a disulfide that ties the N-terminus over the binding pocket would explain loss of function. ClinVar: pathogenic, single submitter.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence, phenotypic spectrum, and modes of inheritance of gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor mutations in idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: COS-7 cells transiently transfected with complementary DNAs encoding the human GNRHR containing each of these four novel mutations failed to respond to GnRH agonist stimulation.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function. Cys279 (6.47) is the cysteine of the CWxP motif of helix 6, next to the Trp280 toggle residue and fully buried (relative solvent accessibility 0.01). Tyrosine is too large for this position. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence, phenotypic spectrum, and modes of inheritance of gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor mutations in idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: COS-7 cells transiently transfected with complementary DNAs encoding the human GNRHR containing each of these four novel mutations failed to respond to GnRH agonist stimulation.

nodes.description: Partial loss of function through reduced GnRH affinity. Extracellular loop 1 (generic number 23.49). In the active pig structure the equivalent glutamine is 5.8 angstroms from GnRH and its side chain hydrogen-bonds to the backbone of extracellular loop 2; arginine there would put a positive charge at the mouth of the pocket, which GnRH enters with its own Arg8. The commonest disease allele: gnomAD v4.1 allele frequency 0.0035 with 10 homozygotes. Homozygotes described clinically have mild disease, including the fertile eunuch form with later reversal and a woman with spontaneous pregnancy. A founder allele, and at a minor allele frequency of 0.029 in Maltese newborns it is ten times commoner there than globally. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: Two novel mutations in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor gene in Brazilian patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and normal olfaction.
evidence.snippet: in vitro analysis indicated that the mutant receptor was able to bind GnRH, but with a reduced affinity

evidence.reference_title: The fertile eunuch variant of idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: spontaneous reversal associated with a homozygous mutation in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor.
evidence.snippet: associated with a homozygous mutation (Gln106Arg) in the GnRH-R

nodes.description: Complete loss of function by misfolding and endoplasmic reticulum retention; fully rescuable by pharmacoperones in cells and in a knock-in mouse. Glu90 (2.53) is buried in the helix bundle (relative solvent accessibility 0.02 in the AlphaFold model). In the active pig structure its side chain hydrogen-bonds to Ser124 and the Met125 backbone on helix 3, in agreement with the mutagenesis study that excluded a salt bridge to Lys121. Lysine reverses the charge in a packed polar pocket between helices 2, 3 and 6. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular basis of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: restoration of mutant (E(90)K) GnRH receptor function by a deletion at a distant site.
evidence.snippet: Transient expression of the mutant E(90)K receptor in COS-7 cells resulted in a virtual abolition of GnRH agonist binding and agonist-stimulated phosphoinositide turnover

evidence.reference_title: Glu(2.53(90)) of the GnRH receptor is part of the conserved G protein-coupled receptor structure and does not form a salt-bridge with Lys(3.32(121)).
evidence.snippet: Models showed that congenital Glu2.53(90)Lys and Glu2.53(90)Asp mutations disrupt interactions with Ser3.35(124) and Trp6.48(280) respectively

nodes.description: Complete loss of function by misfolding, partially rescuable by pharmacoperones. Leu266 (6.34) is on the buried face of the cytoplasmic half of helix 6 (relative solvent accessibility 0.08), 7 angstroms from Gq. Arginine introduces a charge into the packed interface between helices 5 and 6. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence, phenotypic spectrum, and modes of inheritance of gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor mutations in idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: COS-7 cells transiently transfected with complementary DNAs encoding the human GNRHR containing each of these four novel mutations failed to respond to GnRH agonist stimulation.

nodes.description: Loss of binding. Pro282 (6.50) is the proline of the CWxP motif that kinks helix 6, the helix that swings outward on activation. Arginine removes the kink-forming residue and adds a charge 4.5 angstroms from the ligand site. Pro282Leu at the same residue is in ClinVar as likely pathogenic (VCV001709893).

evidence.reference_title: Congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism due to GnRH receptor mutations in three brothers reveal sites affecting conformation and coupling.
evidence.snippet: The Pro282Arg mutant is unable to bind radiolabeled GnRH analogue.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function, not rescuable by pharmacoperones. Ser168 (4.54) is on helix 4 within the membrane; its hydroxyl hydrogen-bonds back to the helix backbone (Trp164, Ile165). Arginine places a charged side chain in the lipid-embedded part of the helix, a change the membrane does not accommodate. Absent from gnomAD v4.1. ClinVar: pathogenic, multiple submitters.

evidence.reference_title: Complete hypogonadotropic hypogonadism associated with a novel inactivating mutation of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor.
evidence.snippet: When introduced into the complementary DNA coding for the GnRH-R, this mutation resulted in the complete loss of the receptor-mediated signaling response to GnRH.

evidence.reference_title: Human loss-of-function gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor mutants retain wild-type receptors in the endoplasmic reticulum: molecular basis of the dominant-negative effect.
evidence.snippet: Mutants hGnRHR(E90K), hGnRHR(L266R), and hGnRHR(S168R) were selected for study because they are known to be fully rescuable, partially rescuable, or nonrescuable (respectively) by a specific pharmacological chaperone.

nodes.description: Complete loss of function. Tyr283 (6.51) lines the hormone pocket: 2.8 angstroms from GnRH in the active pig structure, where it contacts pGlu1, His2 and Trp3 of the hormone, and 3.1 angstroms from elagolix in the human structure. Tyr284Cys (6.52, ClinVar VCV000016025), the neighbouring residue and also a GnRH contact, is a partial loss-of-function allele. ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic.

evidence.reference_title: Role of gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor mutations in patients with a wide spectrum of pubertal delay.
evidence.snippet: In vitro analysis of novel variants (p.Y283H and p.V134G) demonstrated complete inactivation.
